evidence_type: read-only source audit; no GPU admission or performance evidence
current_scope: FP32 1D C2C forward out-of-place; single upload; boost=1; ordered radix 2/4/8/16/32; one uniform logical R through 256; power-of-two grouped batch; N through 8192
prototype_limits: frontier_search/candidate.hpp:30-47 accepts one R and restricts radix, N, R and G; :70-88 requires boost=1 and derives layout from N/R and G.
expanded_search/prepare_headers.py:33-67 replaces register selection before dependent planning, requires one upload and no Rader/Bluestein, and disables the min-R stage reorder.
These are experimental prototype restrictions, not a proof of VkFFT or hardware limitations.

uncovered.finding: VkFFT indexes registers_per_thread_per_radix by radix value. Different radix values may have different logical register counts; repeated equal radix values share an entry.
uncovered.required_work: Inject a full per-radix table before deriving min/max R, stages, thread layout, stage shuffles and first/last IO. Revisit the prototype's disabled min-R reorder; record requested and actual order. Validate all outputs and input immutability independently.
uncovered.priority: First candidate for extending layout choices on the existing power-of-two workload matrix; no claimed speedup.

uncovered.finding: The current independent CPU reference already supports factors 2/3/5, but the frontier request model does not. Factor 7 is not supported by that reference.
uncovered.required_work: Start with 2/3/5-smooth lengths whose observed original plans use no Rader/Bluestein. Generalize divisibility and register tables, handle scheduler radix merging, and recompute all dependent planning. Merely relaxing the whitelist is insufficient. Keep large-prime Rader/Bluestein in a separate domain.
uncovered.priority: Useful next workload-domain extension, sharing register-table infrastructure with the preceding item.

uncovered.finding: Boost interacts with split selection, appended stages, logical storage and block layout. Requested configuration and effective boost need not agree.
uncovered.required_work: Express boost before pass/split selection; validate full resulting stage sequence and effective boost. Replace current boost=1-only N/R and shared-memory assumptions with path-correct derivations. Re-admit generated code and numerical behavior.
uncovered.priority: After a consistent register-table planning contract; higher implementation risk.

uncovered.finding: The current one-kernel candidate model cannot describe a full multi-pass plan.
uncovered.required_work: Specify and validate split products before scheduling, then represent per-pass radix/R/G. Record and verify temporary buffers, reorder, stride and inter-pass layout relationships; measure the complete execution sequence and validate end-to-end outputs.
uncovered.priority: Higher engineering cost; prioritize earlier if large-N workloads are the research target.

uncovered.parameter: independent registers for repeated equal-radix stages
uncovered.finding: This differs from the existing per-radix table: stageRadix indexing cannot distinguish two occurrences of the same radix.
uncovered.required_work: Change the data model and all dependent code generation, storage allocation, shuffle and first/last IO consumers. Do not represent this as a simple configuration override.
uncovered.priority: Highest implementation risk among these extensions.

reporting_rule: Budgeted search results concern only the measured prototype domain. Neither no improvement nor an observed best candidate proves a global VkFFT optimum. These extensions remain unmeasured until separate correctness admission and independently confirmed performance experiments.
